cohort: The study analyzed national vital statistics data encompassing stillbirths and live-births in the United States.
finding: U.S. stillbirth rates plateaued after 2006, with persistent differential risk profiles for early (20-27 weeks) versus late (28+ weeks) stillbirths.
cross-section timing: Data was analyzed for the period 2000 to 2017, with specific comparisons made between 2000-2002 and 2015-2017.
